title: Basic Law Enforcement Academy
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units

program.section_heading: Basic Law Enforcement Academy, Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: Define and recognize the fundamental duties, obligations, and philosophies of the criminal justice system, and function within the law enforcement field.
Define and recognize situations and scenarios relating to application of the California Penal Code, California Health and Safety Code, and the California Vehicle Code, and apply the appropriate law.
Define and recognize the techniques of crime scene searches, courtroom demeanor, and criminal investigation related to child abuse and sexual assault situations.

notes: The REQUIREMENTS tab's course table is not in the supplied text; the text appears cut off mid-sentence ('For information regarding the POST'). The block was built from the prose stating the academy 'consists of two courses': POSC V01A (80-hour orientation) and POSC V01 (910-hour academy), with POSC V01A taken before POSC V01. Check the requirements table for units and total.

No units are printed beside either course, so their units are null. The hours given (80 and 910) are contact hours of credit courses, not the award's measure; measure stays 'units'. The state file stores 32 units for POSC V01 and 3.5 for POSC V01A.
No certificate total is printed in the supplied text; total_units is null.
Outcomes were taken from the outcomes tab. The overview prints the same three PSLOs with lowercase 'California health and safety code' and 'California vehicle code'.
The overview also lists 15 measurable skills and abilities from the RBC's 42 learning domains. These are course-of-study objectives, not program outcomes, and were not recorded as outcomes.
Careers were taken from the program description and the qualifying requirements text. 'reserve officer' is named there as an alternative path for applicants under 21.
